entries.description:
Bytes, held as bytes. The text form of a BinaryData is its base64, which is what String() returns and what New BinaryData(text) reads back, so a value written as text and read again keeps its bytes. Text that is not base64 is refused rather than stored as nothing.

Size() is the number of bytes. Read(path) replaces the bytes with the whole file. Write(path) puts them in a file. A path is not a constructor argument: a string there already means base64.
entries.parameters: base64 — the bytes spelled in base64. Left out, the value is empty.

entries.description: The bytes as base64 text. An empty BinaryData gives an empty string. Anything that is not a BinaryData is refused.
The BinaryData a base64 string spells. An empty string gives an empty BinaryData. Text that is not base64, including spaces, is refused.

The bytes of a string in the encoding given. UTF-8 when the encoding is left out. No byte-order mark is written: a mark belongs at the head of a file, and TextWriter puts one on a UTF-16 file. Text that cannot be written in that encoding is refused.
entries.parameters:
text — the string.
encoding — a TextEncoding value. UTF-8 when it is left out.

entries.description: The string the bytes spell in the encoding given. UTF-8 when the encoding is left out. A byte-order mark at the head of UTF-8 or UTF-16 is a mark, not a character. Bytes that are not text in that encoding are refused.
entries.parameters:
data — a BinaryData.
encoding — a TextEncoding value. UTF-8 when it is left out.
